entry.evidence: Comparing location accuracy for 3D seismic velocity models tends to be problematic because each model is usually determined using different inversion parameters and ray-tracing algorithms.

steps.action: Pose the problem that 3D velocity models cannot be compared fairly for location accuracy because each was built with its own ray tracer and inversion parameters.
steps.quote: Comparing location accuracy for 3D seismic velocity models tends to be problematic

steps.action: Take from Rowe et al. (2009) the result that predicting travel times with a ray tracer other than the model's own degrades the predictions.
steps.quote: almost always results in poor travel-time prediction compared to those predictions determined using the original algorithm

steps.action: Cite the earlier common-model-format approach of Reiter et al. (2012), which forces one predictor on every model.
steps.quote: Fitting various 3D models into a common model format has been attempted with significant effort

steps.action: Propose the 3DTTLS framework: station/phase lookup surfaces populated with travel-time predictions from each model's own ray-tracing algorithm.
steps.quote: we describe the development of a framework to populate 3D station/phase-specific travel-time lookup surfaces (3DTTLS)

steps.action: Describe the IDC's legacy SSSC lookup format and its limits: a lat/lon grid with pole problems, corrections not equidistant from a station, and a single depth.
steps.quote: The SSSC format does not allow for variations in corrections with depth

steps.action: Use the authors' group's earlier tools: the PCalc prediction calculator, GeoTess tessellated grids, and the Bender pseudo-bending ray tracer.
steps.quote: To produce full 3D travel-time lookup surfaces, we use the PCalc program

steps.action: Build 3DTTLS as GeoTess corrections to ak135 with depth variation and path-dependent uncertainty, for first-P and first-S, with station-distance tolerance and user-defined variable gridding.
steps.quote: 3DTTLS are created for each relevant station/phase combination.

steps.action: Design the accuracy test against full 3D ray tracing in SALSA3D: 1000 random pseudo-events between 75°S and 75°N at crustal depths, 157 IMS stations, giving 91,955 first-P and 65,037 first-S paths.
steps.quote: To compare prediction differences between 3DTTLS and 3D ray tracing, 1000 pseudo

steps.action: Set the grid conditions (0.5° spacing to 20°, 1° beyond; constant 2.5 km and 5 km depth spacing; topography included) and build a seismicity-depth model from the ISC catalog to bound depths.
steps.quote: 3DTTLS were created for several grid sizes and depth spacings to investigate possible preferred optimized grid setups.

steps.action: Compare lookup and ray-traced travel times by distance: first-P differences are a few to tens of ms; first-S differences are larger, with high standard deviation out to about 25° and variations near the triplication distance.
steps.quote: Reducing depth spacing to 2.5 km shows a significant decrease in TTD values

steps.action: Because the first-S mismatch was attributed to unresolved small-scale structure, refine the surfaces with variable depth spacing (finer at shallow depths) and 0.5° lateral spacing to 25°.
steps.quote: we decided to create another version of the 3DTTLS with a finer depth spacing and a 0.5° lateral spacing to 25° distance

steps.action: Recompare with the refined surfaces: first-P mean 2.8 ± 68.4 ms; first-S mean similar to the 2.5 km case, with a slightly better median and spread.
steps.quote: For first-S, the mean (136.2 ± 307.7 ms) is similar to the 2.5 km depth spacing example

steps.action: Relocate 2279 GT5 validation events with LocOO3D, using full 3D ray tracing and using 3DTTLS with the same 1D distance-dependent uncertainty, and compare mislocations event by event.
steps.quote: The relocation run using the full 3D ray tracing is slightly favored (51.9%) over the run using 3DTTLS (48.1%)

steps.action: Characterize storage (1.30 GB first-P, 1.09 GB first-S for 157 stations) and single-processor relocation time: about 1.42 times ak135, versus 3-4 orders of magnitude slower for full ray tracing.
steps.quote: the use of 3DTTLS for locations results in very similar times as those for a 1D model

steps.action: Repeat the timing test on a larger independent set, 14,565 IDC LEB events from 2020-2021, which run about 1.25 times slower than ak135.
steps.quote: We also tested calculation times using 3DTTLS for a much larger set of events to confirm the above results.

steps.action: Build surfaces for other models (RSTT natively; DETOX-P2 with Bender; LLNL-G3D with its own ray tracer via exported grid points) to show the framework carries over.
steps.quote: To demonstrate how various models can be used to generate 3DTTLS

steps.action: Pose two questions any user should answer before comparing 3D models: was the model built for location accuracy, and do its developers supply a travel-time and uncertainty predictor?
steps.quote: These questions would need to be answered prior to using any 3D model for comparing seismic location accuracy.

steps.action: Keep the framework as characterized: travel times comparable to full ray tracing depending on the grid, comparable relocations, 1D-like speed, and a preferred grid setup.
steps.quote: Comparisons of travel-time predictions using the 3DTTLS show comparable values to full 3D ray tracing, depending on the grid layout.

tree.answer: No natural phenomenon; a methodological inconsistency in comparing 3D models
Yes: lookup and ray-traced travel times are computed and differenced directly
Build and characterize a fast lookup-surface method that uses each model's own ray tracer
No rival hypotheses; alternative approaches (common predictor, SSSC, full ray tracing) are argued against or used as references
Set computationally: grid spacing, depth spacing, and synthetic event sets
Yes, after refining for first-S: holds across depth spacings, in GT5 relocations, and in a larger LEB timing set
Framework kept as a characterized capability
No review file supplied; not documented

end.claim: 3D travel-time lookup surfaces built in GeoTess with a model's own ray tracer reproduce full 3D ray-tracing travel times (ms-level for first-P, about 100 ms for first-S) and relocations (51.9% vs 48.1% best-located GT5 events) at computation times near those of a 1D model.

decisive_move.sentence: The claim rests on the direct comparison of lookup-surface travel times with full 3D ray tracing over about 157,000 paths, refined until the differences were small.

gates.evidence: No hypothesis directed the data acquisition; the synthetic paths and grids were chosen to characterize the method (§4 ¶2-3). The travel-time and relocation comparisons could have shown large mismatches, and first-S partly did, which prompted the refinement (§4 ¶6-7). No grid choice, threshold, or acceptance criterion was fixed before the comparisons; the grid setup was chosen after them (§7 ¶1).

imports.item: triangular tessellation of the sphere with variable resolution (via GeoTess) in place of a regular lat/lon grid

limits: No review file, discussion, or earlier version was supplied, so there is no review sequence; the acknowledgements thank anonymous reviewers, and the paper was revised (September 2022) without a record of the changes. The composition is coded none_fits because the walk enters on a methodological problem and proceeds by design, test, and refine of an engineering capability; no phenomenon is established and no rival hypotheses are posed, so capability_first does not fit strictly. Sub-claims: the relocation equivalence (capability_characterized) is shown only for first-P, and first-S relocations are not tested; the 51.9/48.1 split has no significance test; the timing claims (capability_characterized) come from one machine, and the authors note that timing tests can be inconsistent. The claim that 3DTTLS would add 'the accuracy and precision of a full 3D model' rests on cited earlier work (Begnaud et al. 2020a, 2021), not on this paper. The benefit of path-dependent uncertainty in relocation is asserted but not tested, since both relocation runs used 1D distance-dependent uncertainty. The central motivation, fair comparison of different 3D models, is argued but never exercised: no location accuracy is compared across models. Figure 16 shows only surfaces for RSTT, DETOX-P2 and LLNL-G3D, with no accuracy check, so the generalization check is weak (inference). Because of that weakness, the computed triangulation (method, replication, generalization) overstates the support (inference). The refined surfaces change lateral and depth spacing together, so their separate effects are confounded. The text gives the first-P 5 km median as '17.7 ± 27.3 s', whereas Table 1 implies ms, an apparent typo.

disagreements.target: Reiter et al. (2012) common-parameterization model comparison using the Podvin-Lecomte ray tracer
disagreements.support: The paper argues, citing Rowe et al. (2009) on degraded predictions from non-native ray tracers, that a common ray tracer biases location comparison; it does not test this directly.
disagreements.quote: This use of a common ray-tracing algorithm, unfortunately, can create an inconsistency when comparing models for location accuracy.

disagreements.target: IDC source-specific station corrections (SSSCs) on a regular lat/lon grid
disagreements.support: The paper illustrates pole distortion and non-equidistant corrections (Fig. 1 vs Fig. 3) and notes that SSSCs hold a single depth.
disagreements.quote: The SSSC format does not allow for variations in corrections with depth

disagreements.target: Position that 3D models' computational requirements make their operational use prohibitive
disagreements.support: Timing tests on 2279 GT5 events and 14,565 LEB events show 3DTTLS relocations within 1.25-1.42 times the 1D ak135 times.
disagreements.quote: For a relatively static network like the IMS, 3DTTLS could be used for standard location calculations as quickly as a 1D model

alternatives_considered.chosen: Model-specific ray tracer populating lookup surfaces
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Common model format with one predictor for all models (Reiter et al.)
alternatives_considered.reason: A common predictor creates an inconsistency and possible bias from parameterization and ray tracer

alternatives_considered.chosen: GeoTess triangular tessellation with depth nodes
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Regular lat/lon SSSC grid at a single depth
alternatives_considered.reason: Avoids pole problems, gives equidistant positions, allows depth variation
Crustal phases require additional theory and study for accurate ray paths and travel times

alternatives_considered.chosen: Pseudo-events between 75°S and 75°N at crustal depths
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Events including polar latitudes; deeper events
alternatives_considered.reason: Avoid concentrating events at the poles; crustal events are more relevant for explosion monitoring

alternatives_considered.chosen: Variable depth spacing (finer shallow), bounded by the seismicity-depth model
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Constant 5 km and 2.5 km depth spacing
alternatives_considered.reason: Most efficient for file size and resolution

alternatives_considered.chosen: Finer depth spacing only at shallow depths
alternatives_considered.reason: Not efficient, since vertical heterogeneity is greater at lithospheric depths than deeper
High first-S standard deviation and variations out to about 25°

alternatives_considered.chosen: 1D distance-dependent uncertainty for both relocation runs
alternatives_considered.reason: Path-dependent uncertainty from the 3D covariance matrix is too costly in full ray tracing, so both runs use the same uncertainty for consistency

alternatives_considered.chosen: A unique grid per surface, read once at start
alternatives_considered.alternatives: A common shared grid; reading surfaces as needed

alternatives_considered.chosen: PCalc Bender ray tracer for DETOX-P2
alternatives_considered.reason: The model did not come with a stand-alone ray tracer
